title: Game Day Football Field
seo_title: Football Field Charcuterie Board: Game Day Showpiece & List
description: A football field charcuterie board for 12 to 15: end zones of salami and chorizo, string cheese yard lines and turf of cucumbers, snap peas and grapes.
hook: A full football field you can eat, from end zone to end zone.
why: The turf is just rows: green rows of cucumbers, snap peas, grapes and broccoli, with string cheese for the yard lines. A long narrow board makes the field shape instantly.
The end zones are pepperoni, chorizo and salami, the football is salami, and cheddar and pepper jack cubes fill the sidelines. It's made for Super Bowl parties and tailgates.

timeline.what: Wash and cut all the vegetables, cut the cheese cubes, and make or buy the guacamole, queso and salsa.
Lay the yard lines and the turf.
Add the guacamole band, the football and the end zones.
Warm the queso and fill the sidelines.

faq.q: How do you make a football field charcuterie board?
faq.a: Lay green rows of cucumbers, snap peas and grapes on a long board, add string cheese yard lines, and fill the end zones with cured meats.

faq.q: How many people does it feed?
faq.a: 12 to 15, more if you add wings on the side.

Cut the vegetables and cheese the day before. Refill the sidelines at halftime from the fridge. Keep meat, cheese and cut fruit out no more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. For a long party, build half, keep the refill in the fridge and top it up halfway through.
